newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa eases on origin sales as stg firms.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa eases on origin sales as stg firms.

text.p: London cocoa futures came under renewed origin selling on Monday, mainly prompted by sterling's strength against other European currencies. But volume was thin.
A stronger sterling makes London cocoa futures more attractive for origin hedging against physical sales to other European destinations.
"It's quite a good price for origins," said one trader.
The benchmark March contract ended 12 stg down on the day at 997 stg a tonne, slipping through nearby resistance of 1,000 stg. It ranged between 1,009 and 996 stg during the session.
Volume was thin at 2,497 lots, including 400 lots of AAs on December.
Traders calculated that the CFTC Commitment of Traders Report (CFTC) released on Friday showed a large increase in the net long positions of 4,000 lots.
"In theory it means they'll (longs) have to sell out, but in my view it's friendly. It's showing a turnaround in the States," said the trader.
But industry buyers were absent in London, awaiting first arrivals in West Africa to provide clues on cocoa availability in the rest of the season.
Sentiment was generally bearish ahead of the arrivals, possibly from this week. But players were not getting excited in either direction.
Ivory Coast, which officially opens its cocoa season on Tuesday, but the government has yet to fix farmers' prices.

Traders said a fast start to cocoa sales, which some Ivorian exporters expect to peak around November or December, could frighten the market after having experienced a slow opening last season followed by a record crop.
On the switches Dec/March traded at 29 stg while May/Sept saw deals at 28 stg, traders said.
Technical support for March is pegged at 985 stg, while resistance is at 1,025 stg for an upward break.
